unresolved_entity_provenance_sources: Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 1, p4: Length is one of the three fundamental quantities of mechanics.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 2, p15: Time is fundamental to describing motion.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 4, p65: Velocity is defined as the rate of change of position.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 4, p68: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 5, Eq 5-1: The net force on a body is equal to the product of the body's mass and its acceleration.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 5, p112: Mass is the characteristic of a body that relates a force on the body to the resulting acceleration.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 5, p115: Force is defined as an influence that causes an object to undergo a certain acceleration.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 7, p142: Work is force times displacement.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 7, p149: Kinetic energy is defined as one-half mass times velocity squared.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 8, p172: Power is the rate of doing work.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 8, p178: Energy is conserved, it cannot be created or destroyed.
Halliday Resnick Walker 12th ed. Ch 9, p220: Momentum is defined as mass times velocity.
NIST SI Brochure 9th ed.: The kilogram is defined by fixing h.
NIST SI Brochure 9th ed.: The metre is defined by c = 299792458 m/s.
NIST SI Brochure 9th ed.: The second is defined by Δν_Cs = 9192631770 Hz.
NIST SI Brochure: Joule is N·m, kg·m²/s².
NIST SI Brochure: Newton is kg·m/s², derived from F=ma.
